title: A Breeze of Color
caption: Sunset colours over Kitt Peak National Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Arizona sky glows with vivid colour as the Sun goes down over NSF NOIRLab's Kitt Peak National Observatory (KPNO). The colours come from sunlight scattering on its way through Earth's atmosphere.

KPNO stands in the Arizona-Sonoran Desert, and dry places like this tend to show clearer sunset colours than regions where rain and humid weather arrive almost every day. Heavier particles in the air, such as water vapour, absorb some of the sunlight and wash the colours out. In dry desert air the light reaches our eyes largely unobstructed. Arizona's sparse population helps as well, keeping the air clean and pollution low.

The conditions that sharpen a sunset also help astronomers once it is dark. The hot, cleaner air lets them record sharper data of the visible sky after nightfall, which is part of what makes the site useful for research.

understand.eye: Sunset colours are visible to the naked eye, though camera settings can change how strong they look in a photograph.
